won.source: The federation's own INFERNO pay-per-view broadcast script of 25 June 2006.

note: Won the CWO World Tag Team Championship from champions Partners in Crime inside the Infernal Machine, Anthony Falconi pinning WolfBane with a sledgehammer-assisted reverse Russian legsweep after a brutal, weapon-filled match that hospitalized both champions.

lost.source: The federation's own INFERNO pay-per-view broadcast script of 24 June 2007.

title: cwo-world-6-man-tag-team

won.source: Billed CWO World 6-Man Tag Team Champions, Rankings bulletin of 13 Sep 1998 -- the title reappears after the honest gap the wing's own r007 record notes (last dated 27 Jul 1997).

how: Reappears in the Rankings bulletin by 13 Sep 1998; won date not evidenced.

title: cwo-world-6-man-tag-team

won.source: House Show Results (Week of 10/11/98-10/17/98): "Unit... defeated World 6-Man Tag Team Champions the CPE... when Howard Newton pinned Tyson after the Powerline... The Unit won the CWO World 6-Man Tag Team Championship," house show, Mankato MN, 16 Oct 1998.

how: Won from the CPE, house show, Mankato MN, 16 Oct 1998.
note: Retained over Outlaw Riders' Steele and the Texas Roughriders, house show, Salina KS, 20 Nov 1998.

title: cwo-world-6-man-tag-team

won.source: House Show Results, 21 Nov 1998: "Thomas Family... defeated Unit... when 'Double D' Damian Dagger pinned Howard Newton after the Look and outside interference by Warhawk... Thomas Family won the World 6-Man Tag Team Championships," house show, Topeka KS, 21 Nov 1998.

how: Won from the Unit, house show, Topeka KS, 21 Nov 1998, aided by Warhawk's outside interference.

title: cwo-world-heavyweight
label: Rt Savage

won.source: The federation's own INFERNO pay-per-view broadcast script of 24 June 2007.

note: Won the six-man INFERNAL MACHINE match, eliminating Prince David Tita last, for the vacant CWO World Championship after Nightrain -- the champion Rt Savage himself had injured a week earlier -- was ruled unable to compete.

title: cwo-world-heavyweight
label: Nightrain

won.source: Not directly witnessed; first attested as champion, billed simply as the CWO World Championship, in the federation's own 9 April 2006 broadcast.

note: A later reading (1999) traces the title as far as Allen "Mr. America" Carter's third reign, still in progress at the held record's last-dated 1999 CWO card (NOVEMBER PAIN '99, 28 November 1999); no document in either reading's own record traces the title between that point and Nightrain's own attested reign in 2006. Retained against Brad Wheatley on 9 April 2006.

lost.source: The federation's own FOREVER pay-per-view broadcast script of 30 April 2006.

title: cwo-world-heavyweight
label: Logan

won.source: Not directly witnessed in the held record's served record; already billed as CWO World Heavyweight Champion on this pass's own earliest read document, FEVER, 16 April 2007 -- the win itself, presumably picking up the title the wing's own record left vacant on 29 June 2006, falls in an earlier gap this lane was not assigned to read.

note: First attested as CWO World Heavyweight Champion on FEVER, 16 April 2007, defending it in non-title matches through 21 May 2007 before losing it to Nightrain at MAY-HEM.

lost.source: The federation's own MAY-HEM pay-per-view broadcast script of 27 May 2007.

title: cwo-cruiserweight
label: "Airborne" Marc Fulcrum

won.source: Not directly witnessed; the CWO Cruiserweight Championship's own creation and Marc Fulcrum's first reign predate the held record's captured record. First attested already in his possession at the unification match of 26 September 1999.

note: Unifies the Cruiserweight and Light Heavyweight Championships by defeating Light Heavyweight Champion Wildfire at SEPTEMBER SLAM IV: DO OR DIE; the surviving title carries the Cruiserweight name forward. The held record ends here.

lost.source: The federation's own 14 March 2001 Rankings chart bills the CWO Cruiserweight Championship vacant; no document in the surviving record narrates when or how "Airborne" Marc Fulcrum's own reign ended.

title: cwo-extreme
label: B-Quikk

won.source: Not directly witnessed in the held record's served record; billed "newly won" CWO EXTREME Champion on EXTREME, 15 May 2007, per that broadcast's own dialogue naming a hardcore battle royal win at the federation's own CWO FOREVER pay-per-view, 29 April 2007 -- that pay-per-view is not part of the held record's assigned documents.

note: B-Quikk's first CWO EXTREME Championship reign, won off-page at CWO FOREVER and lost the same night this pass first attests it, EXTREME, 15 May 2007, to Anthony Falconi.

lost.source: The federation's own EXTREME broadcast script of 15 May 2007.

title: cwo-extreme
label: Dave Lupus, the "South London Sidewinder"

won.source: Not directly witnessed; first billed CWO EXTREME Champion in the federation's own EXTREME broadcast of 4 April 2001. No prior CWO EXTREME Championship reign is held in this wing's own record.

note: Retained in a falls-count-anywhere match against Brent "The Ace" Alles on 30 May 2001.

lost.source: The federation's own EXTREME broadcast script of 6 June 2001.

title: cwo-north-american
label: "The Professional" Brian Thompson

won.source: The federation's own EXTREME broadcast script of 30 May 2001 recaps the win, in a 30-minute-plus match against Mondo Gecko at MAY-HEM; the match itself is not part of the surviving record.

note: Retained, non-title, against Major Slayer at the federation's own 9 June 2001 Hartford house show; retained against Brian McTavish on 6 June 2001 after a low blow and an inside cradle, pulling the tights.

title: cwo-north-american
label: Mondo Gecko

won.source: Not directly witnessed; no document in the surviving record traces the title between Maximum Overdrive's own last attested 1999 reign and Gecko's own attested reign here. First billed CWO North American Champion in the federation's own EXTREME broadcast of 11 April 2001, wrestling "The Professional" Brian Thompson to a 20-minute time-limit draw.

note: Retained by disqualification against Johnny Reb on 16 May 2001.

lost.source: The federation's own EXTREME broadcast script of 30 May 2001 recaps the loss, "in a thrilling 30 minute plus match at MAY-HEM against Brian Thompson"; the match itself is not part of the surviving record.

title: cwo-world-tag-team
label: South Street Riot

won.source: The federation's own INFERNO pay-per-view broadcast script of 24 June 2007.

note: Won a Texas Tornado falls-count-anywhere "Iron Team" four-way match against the Fighter Jets, Hell Risers and champions the Falconi Brothers, 3 falls to 2, an instant replay confirming Dave Vincent's own decisive pin, to win the CWO World Tag Team Championship.

title: cwo-world-tag-team
label: Falconi Brothers

won.source: Not directly witnessed; first attested as champions in the federation's own 8 April 2006 broadcast.

note: No document in the held record traces the title between its last recorded 1997 holders, the Deadly Sins, and the Falconi Brothers' own attested reign in 2006; retained against Brent Alles and Mentor on 8 April 2006.

lost.source: The federation's own FOREVER pay-per-view broadcast script of 30 April 2006.

title: cwo-womens
label: Mary Alles

won.source: The federation's own EXTREME broadcast script of 9 May 2001.

note: Won the newly created, vacant championship from German Choklat; retained in a three-way against Choklat and Big Mama Woo at the federation's own 2 June 2001 Indianapolis house show and against Lt. Cammy LeBeau at the federation's own 9 June 2001 Hartford house show.

title: cwo-world-heavyweight
label: "The Avenger" Jesse Ewiak

won.source: Not directly witnessed; the title is billed vacant in the federation's own 14 March 2001 Rankings chart, and Ewiak is first billed CWO World Champion in the federation's own EXTREME broadcast of 4 April 2001. No document in the surviving record shows the actual title win, presumably at the federation's own MARCH MADNESS 2K1 pay-per-view (25 March 2001), which is not part of the surviving record.

note: First billed champion during the 2001 EXTREME MEASURES relaunch.

lost.source: The federation's own MAXIMUM ASSAULT pay-per-view broadcast script of 29 April 2001.

title: cwo-world-tag-team
label: Darknight Express

won.source: Not directly witnessed; no document survives tracing the title between its 1999 holders, Johnny Reb and "Irresistible Assassin" Eddie Fantastic, and the Darknight Express's own 2001 reign. First billed CWO World Tag Team Champions, defending, in the federation's own EXTREME broadcast of 4 April 2001.

note: Retained against Allen Carter and Geoff Bondavarsky on 4 April 2001.

lost.source: The federation's own MAXIMUM ASSAULT pay-per-view broadcast script of 29 April 2001.

title: cwo-television
label: Wildfire

won.source: The federation's own CWO FEVER broadcast of 25 January 2002, Saginaw County Event Center.

how: Pinned El Suicida after the Wildfire Driver, having hit him with a steel chair while Laura distracted the referee.
note: Retained the title against El Suicida in a falls-count-anywhere match on 1 February and by disqualification against Ewiak on 8 February; still champion on the last served card, 10 February 2002.

title: cwo-television
label: El Suicida

won.source: Billed as the newest Television Champion on the FEVER of 25 January 2002; the card on which he won the title is not in the served record.

how: Won on a card that is not in the served record; billed as the newest Television Champion on 25 January 2002 and beaten that night by Wildfire.

title: cwo-ewa-world-tag-team
label: Pit Bosses

won.source: The federation's own CWO FEVER broadcast of 1 February 2002, Nationwide Arena, Columbus.

how: Presented with the belts in the ring by Lawrence Dawson, who took them from a metal briefcase and crowned them "once again" EWA World Tag Team Champions; no earlier reign of the belts is in the served record.
note: The CWO announcers said the titles would not be recognised; the Pit Bosses were billed as EWA Tag Team Champions on 8 and 10 February 2002 and said they meant to unify the belts with the CWO tag titles.
